response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, f.rebtotal, (f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0) AS relgap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rebtotal) AS overall_avg FROM j), g AS (SELECT orderslink, ordertune, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG(relgap) AS avg_relative_gap FROM j GROUP BY orderslink, ordertune) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relative_gap, g.avg_rebate - overall.overall_avg AS margin_above_overall FROM g CROSS JOIN overall WHERE g.avg_rebate > overall.overall_avg ORDER BY margin_above_overall DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The overall average rebate is the mean of rebtotal over all fee rows that match an order (the joined rows), not over all fees rows.
Rows with feerate = 0 or NULL give a NULL relative gap, which AVG ignores. This avoids division by zero.
The margin is the group's average rebate minus the overall average rebate, in absolute terms and unrounded.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the mean of the group-level averages, with each orderslink/order type combination weighted equally, rather than the row-level mean.
